claim: The VBT stimulation framework (Wang et al. 2025) was applied to two surgically treated patients and to synthetic data, for EZN estimation (diagnosis), not for selecting therapeutic stimulation.

bibliographic_record.authors: Wang HE, Dollomaja B, Triebkorn P, Duma GM, Williamson A, Makhalova J, Lemarechal J-D, Bartolomei F, Jirsa V
bibliographic_record.title: Virtual brain twins for stimulation in epilepsy
bibliographic_record.preprint: medRxiv 10.1101/2024.07.25.24310396 (seen in search results; not opened)
bibliographic_record.verified_via: Europe PMC full-text XML (PMC12457187) and pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov, fetched 2026-10-31

supporting_passage: We used the data from two patients who underwent a standard presurgical protocol at La Timone Hospital in Marseille. The first patient is a 23-year-old female diagnosed with left occipital lobe epilepsy. She underwent resective surgery and was nearly seizure-free after surgery, with an Engel Class II outcome. The second patient is a 19-year-old male with left frontal lobe epilepsy. He underwent resective surgery resulting in complete seizure freedom and an Engel Class I outcome.
population_and_design: Methodological modelling study; n=2 adults with drug-resistant focal epilepsy (SEEG-explored, resected) plus synthetic ground-truth simulations; no control group.
endpoint: Model-estimated EZN (epileptogenicity values per VEP region) compared qualitatively with the resected region; Engel class reported as context (P1 Engel II, P2 Engel I; follow-up length not extracted).
reported_observation: Two patients; e.g. for P1 the left lateral occipital cortex (O2) was consistently identified as part of the EZN across three seizures (Results > Virtual brain twins for SEEG stimulation).
authors_inference: Framework is a basis for moving from invasive to non-invasive diagnosis and treatment. Therapeutic use is framed as future work: 'This framework can be further extended to build high-resolution, patient-specific models for future therapeutic interventions.' (Discussion)
contradictions: None found. Minor internal inconsistency: Results (VEP-stimulation workflow) reports 20,284 cortical vertices; Methods (TI electric field) reports 20,484 vertices.
study_family_id: VEP-INS-Marseille-LaTimone (Jirsa/Bartolomei group; patient overlap across VEP papers not reported - to_verify)
